newsitem.title: USA: US MMS extends oil royalty valuation comment time.
newsitem.headline: US MMS extends oil royalty valuation comment time.

text.p: The U.S. Minerals Management Service said Tuesday it will extend the public comment period on setting valuations for royalties paid to the federal government for oil extracted from federal lands.
The public comment period was to close March 25, but has been extended to April 28 in response to requests for additional time, the MMS said.
The agency also said it postponed public meetings scheduled for February 25 in Houston and March 5 in Lakewood, Colorado, on the proposed royalties valuations rulemaking.
"Industry told us they needed additional time," MMS Director Cynthia Quarterman said in a statement.
"They felt they could not adequately prepare for meetings scheduled February 25 and March 5, so we agreed to reschedule those meetings for a future time," Quarterman said.
New dates will be announced later, the MMS said.
The MMS is considering to how change the way it sets oil royalties values, which have been based on oil prices posted by the companies.
The MMS is pursuing back payments from companies for oil produced in California which the MMS said were paid at below the actual market value of the oil.
